nodes.label: Tidal Heating Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Io's orbit is kept slightly eccentric by the Europa-Ganymede resonance, so Jupiter's gravity flexes the moon continuously; that friction melts the interior, letting Io radiate about twice the heat it receives from the Sun and driving its 400+ volcanoes. The same flexing keeps Europa's ocean liquid beneath its ice shell.

nodes.label: Favorites
nodes.rationale: Save/remove/view favorites; localStorage if no auth. Owned by Gamze (accessibility + favorites).

nodes.label: Accessibility Requirements
nodes.rationale: WCAG-oriented: semantic HTML, keyboard nav, focus states, ARIA labels, alt text, contrast.

nodes.label: Responsive Design
nodes.rationale: Works across desktop (1440px+), tablet (768-1439px), mobile (<768px); cards adapt.

nodes.label: Cosmic Explorer
nodes.rationale: Product vision: interactive astronomy discovery platform transforming NASA public data into intuitive exploration experience; core principle 'NASA provides the data; Cosmic Explorer provides the experience'.

nodes.label: NASA Open APIs
nodes.rationale: Primary data source (api.nasa.gov) - APOD, NEO Web Service, Mars Rover Photos, Earth Imagery.

nodes.label: Single Page Application (SPA)
nodes.rationale: Application architecture - SPA navigation model for exploration without leaving the application.

nodes.label: Discovery Experience
nodes.rationale: Application should feel like a modern space-exploration dashboard rather than simply displaying raw NASA API responses.

nodes.label: Filtering
nodes.rationale: Filter by object type, mission, date, distance; multiple filters, clear-all. Owned by Dhruv.

nodes.label: Search
nodes.rationale: Global search with states (initial/loading/results/no results/error), filtering, sorting. Owned by Dhruv.

nodes.label: Sorting
nodes.rationale: Sort options by relevance, name, date, distance, size.

nodes.norm_label: starfield background with central glowing star

nodes.label: Radial Gradient Glow Technique
nodes.rationale: Layered radial gradients (glow + core) with a Gaussian blur filter emulate a luminous star over a near-black (#04050d) night-sky rectangle, giving depth without raster imagery; scattered small white circles of varied radius/opacity seed a starfield backdrop.

nodes.label: Titan planetary sphere with layered radial gradients
nodes.norm_label: titan planetary sphere with layered radial gradients
nodes.rationale: Three stacked radial gradients (warm golden base #ffe0a0->#7a5216, dark limb shading, and a light haze rim) are layered on a single r=245 circle to fake a spherical body with an atmospheric glow, giving depth without any raster texture.

nodes.label: Missions
nodes.rationale: Discover NASA missions, related objects. Owned by Nithin.

nodes.label: Object Details
nodes.rationale: Detail view with image, metadata, favorite, related content, back navigation. Owned by Nithin.

nodes.label: What Counts as AI-Generated
nodes.rationale: Documented: AI-written or AI-refactored submitted code, AI-generated CSS/markup, non-trivial autocomplete blocks. Not regulated: explanations, error-message help, library suggestions, single-token completions.

nodes.label: AI-Assisted Marker Comment
nodes.rationale: Marker comment '// AI-assisted - see AI-USAGE.md #<n>' drops a pointer where AI-assisted code lives so readers can trace it back to its log entry.

nodes.label: AI Usage Entry Template
nodes.rationale: Each entry captures date, member, tool/model (free models only), files touched, verbatim prompt, and what was kept or changed so AI-assisted work stays reviewable.

nodes.label: Data Source Options
nodes.rationale: Default is a public API rich enough for search/detail/filtering, mapped to the app's shape at the boundary; optionally a group may build a small backend (Node/Express or Next.js API routes) as a stretch connecting to week-12 material.

nodes.label: React SPA Baseline
nodes.rationale: Every group must build a React SPA with collection loading (loading/error/empty states), search/filter/sort, routed detail views, persisted user state in a custom hook or Context + localStorage, at least one controlled form, multiple routes, accessibility, responsiveness, public deployment, and automated tests.

nodes.label: Cosmic Explorer
nodes.rationale: Single-page web application for exploring astronomy and space discovery data; team topic for CSCI 3230U.

nodes.label: NASA Open APIs
nodes.rationale: Primary data source chosen because it is NASA's public API platform; specific endpoints to be finalized after evaluating available data for search, filtering, and detailed object views.

nodes.label: CSCI 3230U AI Use Policy
nodes.rationale: Lets students learn to use AI coding tools like professionals while keeping early learning honest and putting no one at a disadvantage.

nodes.label: AI-USAGE.md Log
nodes.rationale: Logs every time an AI tool contributed to submitted code; must be empty until the third milestone because milestones 1-2 (weeks 3, 6) are AI-free.

nodes.label: Grading Scheme (44%)
nodes.rationale: Project is 44% of the final grade: M0 2%, M1 8%, M2 12%, M3 14%, M4 8%.

nodes.label: CSCI 3230U Group Project Requirements
nodes.rationale: Course's major summative assessment (no final exam); staged checkpoints spread the work across the term instead of cramming it into the last two weeks, and every milestone is demoable and graded so progress cannot be deferred.

nodes.label: AI-Free Milestones 1-2
nodes.rationale: Milestones 1-2 (weeks 3, 6) must be written without AI generating code so the early learning stays honest; milestones 3-4 (week 10, final exam week) may use AI.

nodes.label: AI Documentation Requirement
nodes.rationale: AI that produces submitted work must be recorded in AI-USAGE.md with the exact prompt, before commit; documenting honestly is a normal professional habit and the safe choice against academic-misconduct charges.

nodes.label: Explore Page
nodes.rationale: Primary landing experience - hero, search, featured content, categories. Owned by Maryam.

nodes.label: Team Git Workflow
nodes.rationale: Plan with Issues, work on branches, merge through reviewed Pull Requests, keep main protected and green; graded state of each milestone is what is on main at the deadline.

nodes.label: Vertical Slice
nodes.rationale: The unit of contribution: one feature built end-to-end through every layer (UI component, state/hook, data, route, tests + accessibility), owned by one member and visible as their commits and PRs so individual contribution can be judged from Git history.

nodes.label: NASA Open APIs (api.nasa.gov)
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the project's primary data source because it is a publicly available, open API platform; the team will finalize specific endpoints after evaluating available data for search, filtering and detail views, with live integration planned for Milestone 3.

nodes.label: Team Cosmic Explorer
nodes.rationale: Each member owns a vertical slice of the product built on a shared app shell, so ownership is split by feature area rather than by layer.

nodes.label: Accessibility & Responsive Design Requirements
nodes.rationale: Mobile-first layout, WCAG AA contrast, semantic HTML, keyboard navigation and screen-reader support are required so the product is usable by everyone; these constraints shape the markup and CSS choices throughout the prototype.

nodes.label: Favourites Persisted in localStorage
nodes.rationale: Favourites are stored client-side in localStorage so users can keep objects they find and have them accessible across sessions without requiring a backend account system.

nodes.label: React + Vite Migration (M2/M3)
nodes.rationale: The course brief requires each team to build a single-page application with a searchable, filterable card collection, detail pages, favourites and API-loaded data, so the static HTML/CSS prototype is deliberately rebuilt as a React + Vite app with live NASA data, client-side routing and tests across milestones M2 and M3.

nodes.label: Encouraged AI Workflow
nodes.rationale: Do it yourself first so you learn, then delegate repetitive or boilerplate work, and always review and verify - you own every line you submit and may be asked to explain any part of the project.

nodes.label: Free Models Only Rule
nodes.rationale: Only AI tools without a paid plan may be used because no one should need to spend money for the course; the model used cannot be verified, but undocumented AI code is an integrity violation.

nodes.label: M4 - Independent Concept & Short-Form Video
nodes.rationale: Research a concept not taught in the course (each group's concept is unique), integrate a working example, and explain it in a ~1-3 min short-form video.

nodes.label: CosmicObject
nodes.rationale: Normalized model with id, name, type, description, imageUrl, date, mission, metadata, source - allows components to work across APIs.

nodes.label: ObjectCard
nodes.rationale: Reusable component displaying image, name, category, description, metadata, favorite button, view details.

nodes.label: API Fallback/Sample Data
nodes.rationale: Support sample/mock data if NASA API unavailable so app remains usable for dev/testing/demo.

nodes.label: Centralized API/Data Layer
nodes.rationale: Do not allow individual UI components to directly handle raw NASA API responses. Use centralized api/services layer.

nodes.label: Data Normalization
nodes.rationale: Different NASA APIs return different schemas; frontend must not depend on raw schema. Normalize to common CosmicObject model.
